title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts: Collection Limits, Small-Balance Write-Off and Employer Credit
content:
Benefit Overpayment Accounts close out on these figures, set by the classification of each account.

| Classification | Years after the determination date after which recovery stops and the balance is written off | Small-balance write-off threshold (USD) | Months without any recovery before a small balance is written off | Recovered principal credited back to charged employers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Agency Error | 6 | 10.00 | 12 | Yes |
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Employer Reporting Error | 6 | 10.00 | 12 | Yes |
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Appeal Reversal | 6 | 10.00 | 12 | Yes |
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Claimant Error | 10 | 10.00 | 12 | Yes |
| Fraud Overpayment — First Offense | 15 | 0.00 | 0 | Yes |
| Fraud Overpayment — Repeat Offense | 15 | 0.00 | 0 | Yes |

## Reading the figures

- A small-balance threshold of 0.00 and an inactivity figure of 0 mean that the balance is never written off as a small balance; both fraud classifications read this way.
- The small-balance threshold is the balance below which a debt that has had no recovery for the inactivity months is written off.

**Questions answered.**

*How long is a Non-Fraud Overpayment — Claimant Error balance pursued?* 10 years after its determination date.

*Is principal recovered on a Fraud Overpayment — First Offense account credited back to charged employers?* Yes; every classification credits recovered principal back to the charged employers.
